sentences.text: Record shows that in respect of an incident, which is alleged to have occurred on 15.01.2023, a delayed F.I.R. dated 01.02.2023 was lodged by first informant/prosecutrix namely Sahenoor and was registered as Case Crime No. 46 of 2023, under Sections 376, 504, 506, 228-A IPC, Sections 5/6 POCSO Act and Section 67 I.T. Act, P.S. Thakurdwaras, District Moradabad.
In the aforesaid F.I.R., applicant Mahfooj has been nominated as solitary named accused.
The gravamen of the allegations made in the F.I.R. is to the effect that applicant Mahfooj is a teacher of the prosecutrix.
Taking advantage of the relationship of teacher and taught, applicant is alleged to have dislodged the modesty of the prosecutrix since the prosecutrix was a student of class VI/VII.

The F.I.R. further records that the applicant is alleged to have snapped obscene photographs of the prosecutrix and in the garb of the same, continued to dislodge the modesty of the prosecutrix by extending threat.

Subsequently, the obscene photographs of the prosecutrix came to the knowledge of the husband of the prosecutrix, who was subsequently married and on account of above, the husband of the prosecutrix refused to maintain her.

After above mentioned F.I.R. was lodged, Investigating Officer proceeded with statutory investigation of concerned case crime number in terms of Chapter XII Cr. P.
C.
The statement of the prosecutrix was recorded under Section 161 Cr. P. C., wherein the prosecutrix has clearly supported the F.I.R.
Same is on record at page 23 of the paper book.
Thereafter, the prosecutrix was requested for her internal medical examination.

However, the Doctor, who examined the prosecutrix did not find any Mahfooj vs State Of U.P. on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111805242/
2 external injury on her body so as to denote commission of sexual assault.

Thereafter,
the statement of the prosecutrix was recorded under Section 164 Cr. P. C., wherein she has rejoined her previous statement recorded under Section 161 Cr. P. C.

The Investigating Officer further examined other witnesses under Section 161 Cr. P. C.
who have also supported the F.I.R. On the basis of above and other material collected by him during the course of investigation.
Investigating Officer came to the conclusion that complicity of applicant is fully established in the crime in question.
He, accordingly, submitted the charge sheet dated 30.3.2023, whereby applicant has been charge sheeted under Sections 376, 504, 506, 228-A IPC, Sections 5/6 POCSO Act and Section 67 I.T. Act.
After aforementioned F.I.R. was lodged, the prosecutrix on account of the facts as noted above is alleged to have committed suicide on 14.3.2023.

Thereafter, another F.I.R. dated 14.3.2023 was lodged by Mohammad Abid (brother of the deceased) and was registered as Case Crime No. 64 of 2023, under Section 306 IPC, P.S. Dilari, District Moradabad.
In the aforesaid F.I.R. Imran (the husband of the deceased) has been nominated as solitary named accused.
The gravamen of the allegations made in the F.I.R. is to the effect that earlier an F.I.R. was lodged against Mahfooj for having dislodging the modesty of the sister of the first informant.
On account of aforesaid fact, the husband of the deceased continuously harassed her.
Named accused further refused to maintain her.
Therefore, she ultimately committed suicide.

After aforementioned F.I.R. was lodged, Investigating Officer proceeded with statutory investigation of concerned case crime number in terms of Chapter XII Cr. P.
C.

He examined first informant and other witnesses under Section 161 Cr. P. C.,
wherein the complicity of applicant Mahfooj emerged in the crime in question.
As per the inquest report (panchayatnama) of the deceased, it was opined by the witnesses of inquest (panch witnesses) that the nature of death of the deceased is suicidal.
Similar view was taken by the Autopsy Surgeon, who conducted autopsy of the body of the deceased.
Except for the ligature mark, no other ante mortem injury was found on the body of the deceased by Autopsy Surgeon.

Learned counsel for applicant with reference to the facts of the first case crime number submits that applicant is a named accused in the F.I.R. dated 1.2.2023,
whereas not named in the F.I.R. dated 14.3.2-23.
However, the applicant has been charge sheeted in both the case crime numbers.
With reference to the F.I.R. dated 1.2.2023, the learned counsel for applicant contends that as per the recital contained in the F.I.R. dated 1.2.2023, the F.I.R. itself is highly belated.
However, neither in the F.I.R. nor in the statement of the first informant, the delay in lodging the F.I.R. has been sufficiently explained.

He, therefore, submits that since the delay in lodging the F.I.R. has not been sufficiently explained, therefore, the prosecution of the applicant Mahfooj vs State Of U.P. on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111805242/
3 itself cannot be maintained.
It is then contended that the medical evidence does not support the ocular version of the occurrence.
Much emphasis was laid to the recital contained at page 28 of the paper book pertaining to Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 30761 of 2023.

sentences.text: The statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Sections 161/164 Cr. P. C. are not worthy of credit as prima facie they are false.

Even otherwise,
applicant is a man of clean antecedents having no criminal history to his credit except the present one.
Applicant is a teacher by profession.
He has been falsely and maliciously implicated in the crime in question.
Applicant is in jail since 30.2.2023.
As such, he has undergone, more than 6 1/2 months of incarceration.
The police report i.e. charge sheet in terms of Section 173 (2) Cr. P. C. has already been submitted.
As such, the entire evidence sought to be relied upon by the prosecution against applicant stands crystallized.
Upto this stage, no such circumstance has emerged on the basis of which, it can be said that the custodial arrest of applicant is absolutely necessary during the pendency of trial.
In respect of the F.I.R. dated 14.3.2023, the learned counsel for applicant contends that applicant is innocent.
Applicant is not named in the F.I.R.

The complicity of the applicant in the crime in question has emerged as per the statements of the witnesses examined under Section 161 Cr. P. C., wherein the facts pertaining to the earlier F.I.R.
have been reiterated.

According to the learned counsel for applicant, from the material collected upto this stage, it cannot be definitely concluded that applicant has abetted, instigated or conspired in the commission of the crime in question.

In short,
the submission is that none of the ingredients of Section 107 IPC is satisfied against the applicant.
He has again rejoined rest of the submissions urged by him in support of the bail application relating to F.I.R. dated 1.2.2023.
Per contra, the learned A.G.A. and the learned counsel for first informant have vehemently opposed the prayer for bail.
They submit that since applicant is a named/not named but charge sheeted accused, therefore, he does not deserve any indulgence by this Court.

With reference to the material on record, they contend that it is an undisputed fact that applicant was the teacher, whereas the prosecutrix was his pupil and there was teacher and taught relationship in between the applicant and the prosecutrix.
Taking advantage of the sacred relationship, applicant has dislodged the modesty of the prosecutrix from the date when the prosecutrix was a young and innocent girl, a student of Class VIth.

The applicant has been charge sheeted under the provisions of Section 67 of I.T. Act, which clearly goes to show that some obscene material must have been recovered by the Investigating Officer during the course of investigation.

It is further admitted that irrespective of the act of applicant, the marriage of the prosecutrix was solemnized with one Imran but when the obscene photographs/obscene vedios of the prosecutrix came to the knowledge of the husband of the prosecutrix, he abandoned the prosecutrix.
It was in the light of above, that prosecutrix committed suicide.
On the above, premise, it is thus urged that instigation is explicit against applicant by conduct.

In support of above, reliance is placed upon the judgement of the Supreme Court in Ranganyaki Vs. State, 2004 Mahfooj vs State Of U.P. on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111805242/
4 (12) SCC 571, wherein it has been held that instigation can be inferred against accused by his conduct.

sentences.text: The death of the deceased has occurred just after two months from the date of earlier F.I.R. dated 15.1.2023, which also goes to show the proximity in between the disclosure of the obscene photographs/videos of the prosecutrix of the deceased.

Upto this stage, neither any such material has emerged on record, on the basis of which it can be inferred that the prosecution story is false nor it can be definitely concluded that applicant is being falsely and maliciously prosecuted.
On the cumulative strength of above, it is urged by the learned A.G.A. as well as the learned counsel for first informant that no indulgence be granted by this Court in favour of applicant.
They, therefore, contend that no good ground exist to enlarge the applicant on bail.
When confronted with above, the learned counsel for applicant could not overcome the same.

Having heard the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for state, the learned counsel for first informant, upon perusal of record, nature of offence,
evidence, complicity of the accused, accusation made, the nature and gravity of offence, coupled with the fact that the prosecutrix in her statements under Sections 161/164 Cr. P. C. has clearly implicated the applicant in the crime in question arising out of F.I.R. dated 1.2.2023, the applicant has breached the sacred relationship in between the applicant and the prosecutrix i.e. teacher and the taught, prima facie the deceased committed suicide on account of act of applicant.

Instigation is writ large against the applicant by his conduct, nothing has been brought on record to establish that the prosecution of the applicant is false or malicious, therefore, irrespective of the submission urged by the learned counsel for applicant, applicant is a man of clean antecedents, the period of incarceration undergone and also the fact that the police report in terms of Section in terms of Section 173 (2) Cr. P. C. has already been submitted
, as such the entire evidence sought to be relied upon by the prosecution against applicant stands crystallized, this Court does not find any good ground to enlarge the applicant on bail.
As a result, bail applications fail and are liable to be rejected.

They are, accordingly, rejected."
5.

Learned counsel for applicant submits that first informant in the case, under Section 376 IPC i.e.
Case Crime No. 46 of 2023, under Sections 376, 504, 506, 228-A IPC, Sections 5/6 POCSO Act and Section 67 I.T. Act, Police Station-Thakurdwara, District-Moradabad has turned hostile.
On the above premise, he, therefore, submits that applicant is liable to be enlarged on bail.
6. Per contra, the learned A.G.A. for State-opposite party-1 has vehemently opposed the prayer for bail.
He submits that the trial of applicant in two different case crime numbers is going on separately.
There is no joint trial of applicant, therefore, the evidence, which has emerged during Mahfooj vs State Of U.P. on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/111805242/
5 course of any trial, can neither be looked into nor it can be relied upon in another trial.

He,
therefore, submits that up to this stage, no new circumstance has emerged on the record of sessions case pertaining to trial of applicant in Case Crime No. 64 of 2023, under Section 306 IPC, Police Station-Dilari, District-Moradabad.
As such, no new, good or sufficient ground has emerged so as to enlarge the applicant on bail.
7. When confronted with above, the learned counsel for applicant could not overcome the same.

8. Having heard, the learned counsel for applicant, the learned A.G.A. for State, upon perusal of record, evidence, nature and gravity of offence, complicity of accused, accusations made coupled with the fact that since the objections raised by the learned A.G.A. in opposition to the present repeat application for bail could not be dislodged by the learned counsel for applicant with reference to the record, therefore, irrespective of the varied submissions urged by the learned counsel for applicant in support of the present repeat application for bail, but without making any comments on the merits of the case, this Court does not find any good or sufficient ground to enlarge the applicant on bail.
9.
As a result, present repeat application for bail fails and is liable to be rejected.
10. It is accordingly rejected.
